captions.detailed: This 3D model is a delta 3D printer effector, featuring a flat, circular central hub with three wide arms extending outward at 120-degree intervals. The central hub contains a large circular opening in the middle for a hotend, surrounded by a radial pattern of eight small mounting holes. Each of the three arms terminates in a cylindrical hinge block with protruding conical nubs and a horizontal mounting hole running parallel to the arm's outer edge.
captions.instruction: Create a parametric delta 3D printer effector in OpenSCAD. The design must feature a central circular body with a large central opening, a radial pattern of M3 mounting holes, and three arms extending outwards at 120-degree angles, each terminating in a cylindrical joint with mounting nubs.
captions.factory: The design is built using three main modules: 'effector', 'body', and 'arm'. The 'body' module uses a hull of two thin cylinders to create a slightly chamfered central disk. The 'arm' module creates flat rectangular extensions using cubes, ending in a cylindrical hinge assembly with conical nubs modeled using rotated cylinders. In the main 'effector' module, a union combines the body and three rotated arms, after which a difference operation subtracts the central hotend cylinder and a radial for-loop of M3 mounting holes.
